A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Spotlight study. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and Appendices A–J support reliable comparison, including matching relocated material and inspecting text embedded in figures.

before.justification: V1 reports original human annotation studies, model evaluations, DPO ablations, and cross-domain experiments in Section 3, Section 6, and the appendices.

after.justification: V3 retains original human-study and model-evaluation results, including the quantitative comparisons and supplementary experiments in Appendix I.

M1.justification: The two-stage procedure remains supervised fine-tuning followed by DPO on the other half of the training data, preferring spotlights over summaries. The model families, DPO objective, prompts, and appendix KTO procedure are unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions use News, CSPubSum, Wikipedia, and Research Presentation for the same tasks and cross-domain evaluations. V3's additional source screenshots illustrate existing datasets rather than establish new coverage.

E2.justification: The corresponding evaluations retain the same traditional baselines, prompted large models, and vanilla, SFT, DPO, and KTO variants. Highlights were already evaluated in v1 Appendix B.3; their appearance in v3 Section 3.3 is not a new comparator.

E3.justification: The reported splits, training budgets, hyperparameters, evaluation metrics, and annotation sample sizes are retained. V1 Table 16 and v3 Table 17 give identical dataset splits; Appendix F preserves the same experimental settings.

E4.justification: The mini-story studies, DPO data-allocation ablations, judge-validation analyses, cross-domain tests, and failure case are retained. Moving v1 Appendix B.3 into the main text and adding dataset-source illustrations do not establish additional analyses.

E5.justification: Both versions retain the same annotation-agreement reporting, McNemar test, DPO significance statements, and correlation analyses. V3 adds no repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or new uncertainty-estimation procedures.

E6.justification: V3 Table 4 explicitly lists highlight percentages of 20%, 28%, 28%, and 16% alongside spotlight percentages already reported in v1 Appendix B.3. Figure 1 also extends the illustrated summary with a generalization sentence. The matched experimental tables otherwise retain their numerical results.

T1.justification: The DPO loss and mathematical definitions underlying the characterization metrics remain unchanged. Neither version introduces additional theorems, proofs, or substantive mathematical derivations.

C1.justification: The central contributions remain a distinct engaging condensation format, four curated datasets, and an SFT-plus-DPO generation approach. V3 foregrounds the existing distinction from highlights without changing the core novelty or headline performance claims.

C2.justification: V3 adds interpretations about the semantic modeling needed for spotlights and states that summary-trained models lose engagement qualities in Section 6(D), which Table 8 does not directly establish. Expanded captions also explain the examples' narrative appeal. The stated limitations and failure mechanisms are retained.

D1.justification: V1 provides a shortened code link in Section 5.3; v3 explicitly names a GitHub repository in the abstract and states that both datasets and code are available. This expands access information, but the PDFs do not establish changed hosted resources. Implementation settings remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The introduction and Appendix E add numerous citations covering dialogue and aspect-based summarization, entity extraction, opinion analysis, and intent detection. These provide brief extensions of the existing positioning rather than a developed new comparison. The persona-summarization paper's publication update represents the same previously cited work.

P1.justification: V3 moves the spotlight–highlight discussion from Appendix B.3 to Section 3.3, expands several explanations and result-discussion paragraphs, and makes localized language and author-credit edits. The overall narrative and section organization remain largely intact.

P2.justification: Figures 1–2 are reformatted, dataset-source screenshots are added as Figures 4–5, and several captions are expanded. Table 4 displays the previously discussed highlight comparison. Most table structures and the overall two-column layout are retained.

improvement.justification: V3 modestly improves accessibility through the main-text highlight comparison, clearer figure labels, source illustrations, and explicit code/data access information. The gains concern presentation and documentation more than experimental support. Added repetition and the unsupported engagement-loss interpretation in Section 6(D) limit the improvement.
